title: Exploring Bengali Religious Dialect Biases in Large Language Models with Evaluation Perspectives
findings: The study found a persistent bias in LLMs towards the Muslim dialect of Bengali over the Hindu dialect. While explicitly mentioning religion in prompts improved accuracy, a notable bias remained, with models often defaulting to Muslim dialect terms even when a Hindu context was specified. The models performed better at inferring religious context from implicit cues rather than explicit mentions but struggled to maintain religious context throughout a conversation (LLM memory). This bias was consistent across various contexts, suggesting it is deeply embedded, likely due to the composition of the training data.
